# Physiome Model Repository

CellML models of the [Physiome Model Repository](https://models.physiomeproject.org) (the exposures in `physiome/models.json`, most of them CellML 1.0 and 1.1 documents, which libcellml reads in its permissive mode). Every model is simulated with [libopencor](https://opencor.ws/libopencor/) over 0 to 100 time units in 1000 steps (`libopencor`, a fine output grid: the models are stiff and many of them switch their right-hand side hard, where the two solvers step over the switch differently on a coarse grid), converted to SBML (`cellml2sbml`), simulated with [sbmlsim-core](https://matthiaskoenig.github.io/sbmlsim-core/) (`sbmlsim`), converted back to CellML (`sbml2cellml`) and simulated with libopencor again (`roundtrip`). See [Development](development.md#physiome) for how to run it.

The repository has no expected results: the `sbmlsim` and the `roundtrip` simulation are compared with the `libopencor` simulation of the model of the repository, over every variable of the model. A value passes when `|value - expected| <= absolute + relative * |expected|` with a relative tolerance of `1e-3` and an absolute tolerance of `1e-6`. Both simulators integrate with CVODE with tight tolerances (relative/absolute `1e-9`/`1e-12`) and up to 100000 internal steps between two time points, so the comparison measures the conversion and not the integrator; only when CVODE gives up with these tolerances the simulation is repeated with `1e-8`/`1e-10` and `1e-7`/`1e-9`. Both simulations scale the absolute tolerance with the smallest initial value of a state of their own model when it is below one: the states of the SBML side are amounts, which are small for a model with a small compartment, and the states of the CellML side the variables of its components.

A `libopencor` failure means libopencor cannot simulate the model of the repository, it says nothing about the converters.

## Timings

Wall time of the simulations which pass or fail, measured inside the simulator wrapper in the worker process, so it holds no overhead of the harness. The setup is everything a simulator does with the model before it integrates: reading and converting the file, compiling the model and building the instance. Both simulators cache what they compiled, so a model simulated again in the same process needs no setup; every case here is set up once. Both of them run the model once before the run of the result, so that the generation of the code of a model, which libopencor does when it runs the model the first time, is part of the setup.

The two simulators integrate with the same relative tolerance and with an absolute tolerance scaled to the states of their own model (amounts for the SBML model, the variables of the components for the CellML model), so neither of them is given an easier problem.

![Integration time of libopencor against sbmlsim-core per case](images/physiome_timings.svg#only-light)
![Integration time of libopencor against sbmlsim-core per case](images/physiome_timings_dark.svg#only-dark)

| stage | simulator | model | simulations | setup median | integration median | integration p95 | integration slowest | integration total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| libopencor | libopencor | CellML model | 62 | 22 ms | 0.87 ms | 76 ms | 506 ms | 1.3 s |
| sbmlsim | sbmlsim-core | SBML model | 60 | 6.0 ms | 1.00 ms | 80 ms | 488 ms | 1.4 s |
| roundtrip | libopencor | roundtrip CellML model | 62 | 18 ms | 0.88 ms | 77 ms | 505 ms | 1.3 s |

The two simulators integrate the same dynamics for 57 cases, those whose SBML model reproduces the expected results. libopencor is 1.3 times faster than sbmlsim-core for the median of them and faster for 51; over these cases the medians are 0.93 ms for sbmlsim-core and 0.60 ms for libopencor.

## Failure reasons

The cases which fail a stage, grouped by their error: errors which differ only in quoted text, numbers and, for the validation of a CellML model, the issues after the first one are one group. Every case is listed with its complete error.

### libopencor

4 of 66 cases fail.

**2 cases**

```text
22e: SimulationFailure: libopencor: SimulationError: run: Task | CVODE: at t = 14.6 and h = 2.02e-05, the corrector convergence test failed repeatedly or with |h| = hmin.
5f0: SimulationFailure: libopencor: SimulationError: run: Task | CVODE: at t = 1.46 and h = 5.6e-10, the corrector convergence test failed repeatedly or with |h| = hmin.
```
